sections.text: Here in Me living as one, O Arjuna, behold the whole universe, movable and immovable, and anything else that thou wouldst see!
न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा।
Yet since with mortal eyes thou canst not see Me, lo! I give thee the Divine Sight. See now the glory of My Sovereignty.
Sanjaya continued: Having thus spoken, O King, the Lord Shri Krishna, the Almighty Prince of Wisdom, showed to Arjuna the Supreme Form of the Great God.

We had been discussing chapter 11, Vishwarupadarshan. We discussed that after listening to the glories of the divine, we, at least as seekers, understand how to see divinity in the world of plurality with respect. But at the same token, we all have the exact same issue: even though I can intellectually appreciate this, even though I can see the argument about the unity of all things, thats not my personal experience. My personal experience is something other than that. I do feel very clearly separated from the world as an entity. And thats exactly Arjunas opening question.
Basically saying that I am completely satisfied with your explanation. Out of your compassion, you give it to me, you explain to me your glory. I also understand that you are the source of everything and you will be the resting place for everything. However, I want to see all that into one. All that vision I need to see. It is a one unified vision where I feel that oneness with this world.
With that request, Bhagavan said, yes, I can show you that because you are ready. A seeker reaches a point where he really wants to know -- and thats where Arjuna is now. Krishna is saying, you are at that point where I can show you this. However, no matter how hard you try, you will not be able to see this with your normal eyes. In other words, the way you are trained or programmed to see this world as separate individuals will not allow you to see the unity. We are programmed right from our birth: this is me, this individual limited being is me, this body and mind-intellect is me.
Our psyche is programmed to see that way. As long as we see the waves in the ocean as individual waves, not part of the ocean, we wont see the unity. Unless you change the perspective, the perception, the paradigm, you will not be able to see the unity. Therefore, you will not be able to see this with your normal eyes. I have to give you a divine Drashti -- divine eyes, another way of looking at this world than you are used to. The same thing can be seen by two different people, and one person sees something in it while the other person sees something else. It all depends on my perspective, on how I see things. You know those riddles: what do you see in this picture? Do you see a glass, or do you see two people facing each other? It depends on whether youre seeing the negative space or the positive space. So Bhagavan said, I need to change your way of seeing, and so I will give you a Divya Drashti.
And we obviously know that at the same time, when Arjuna gets Divya Drashti, Sanjaya automatically gets it too, because he already had the divine vision given to him -- the ability to see whats happening on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. Not only can he see whats happening physically on the battlefield, he can also peer into the minds of the people who are fighting that battle. So he can see what Arjuna sees. He can also feel what Arjuna feels. And he can narrate all of this to his audience. So Bhagavan fulfilled his promise and told Arjuna, I will let you see the cosmic form.
In other words, seeing this entire cosmos as one. Right now, we see the entire cosmos as, at a minimum, two: I and the cosmos. Even though I theoretically know that myself is not outside this cosmos or this world, when I become an observer, I exclude myself from the observed, which is the world. That perception was created the day I was born, when the first thought this is me arose. The I, the ego, was born and associated with this limited being. It excluded me from everything else which I observe as an observer.
And to remove this, I need to first remove the I-ness. So the different perception which Bhagavan is giving him is to combine all these things into one. As we say, the only thing which divides us is the space between you and me, and the time between me and others. Take these two concepts out of my perception, and the world becomes one entity. If there are droplets of water on my table, each droplet has its own existence because it is divided from the other droplet by space.
But we know they came out of the same glass of water. Once the identification with the droplet is developed, two droplets become individuals, and they are apart from each other. Bhagavan said, I need to change your perception. Its not that Im going to change the world -- Im going to change your perception. With this normal, programmed perception of yours, you will never be able to see oneness.
Therefore, temporarily, I want to take this limitation away from you. As long as Im programmed to see this space as room space, I will have difficulty combining it with the universal space outside. But if I change my perception and look at it from outside, then I can combine them. A good example would be: we are walking down Knuckles Road and you can see the trees all separated. You go a little further up to a birds eye view, and the streets start coming together. When you are at 15,000 feet in an airplane flying from Richmond Airport and look down at Richmond, it looks like one big entity -- everything becomes part of it. Right now from ground level, everything is individual. Every building has its own identity, every street has its own identity, every lamp post has its own identity. Just go to 15,000 feet above and have a view -- all these merge into one complex. You go even further up, and all things merge into completely one.
Bhagavan is taking Arjuna into that 25,000-foot view of this cosmos. So then what Arjuna saw, Sanjaya saw through Arjunas eyes and mind. What follows is Sanjayas honest attempt to tell Dhritarashtra what Arjuna is experiencing. Verses 9, 10, and 11 say: Evamuktva tatvarajan Maha Yogeshwaro Harihi Darsaya Maa Saparthaya Paramam Rupam Aishwaram. Having said that Arjuna will not be able to see this with his normal perception, that his perception must change, and that Krishna will help him do that -- now, having said this, O Rajan, O King, the Maha Yogeshwara Hari, because he was the Lord of the Yogas, could do that for Arjuna.
Right now Im connected with my world, with my limited perception, but the Lord of Yoga can change my connection. Maha Yogeshwara Harihi -- Hari is one who removes ignorance. He is the Yogi who can connect this mundane state of existence with that universal state. He is the Lord of Yoga. He showed Arjuna -- Dasaya Masparthaya Paramam Rupam Aishwaram -- the supreme form of his being.
Basically, this just confirmed that Krishna fulfilled his promise to Arjuna to show him the cosmic form. The next verse is Sanjayas quick attempt to paint what he is seeing through Arjunas eyes for Dhritarashtra. So he says Anek Vaktra Nayanam Anek Adhut Darshana. When we are overwhelmed by something, we cant really go into detail about whats happening. Oh, I think theres chaos here. People are running around.
Think of the description of 9/11 -- in the first few hours there is panic, fear, the cloud, the smoke coming out. People are running in the streets. Nobody knows whats happening. But generally, this is what I can say. The first journalist has to narrate to the world whats happening, and if its on radio and not on TV, he can only describe impressions. So Sanjaya says Anek Vaktra Nayanam: I see many mouths and many eyes.
Anek Adbhut Darshanam -- there are so many wonderful sights. Adbhut means something which I have not seen normally. In this one form of the Supreme Being, I see many mouths, many eyes, and many wonderful sights. Anek Divya Abharanam -- many divine ornaments. Divya Aneko Yata Yudham -- and many divine weapons uplifted.
Obviously hes seeing the whole thing on the battlefield, so the first thing that comes to his mind is the weapons. Many mouths, many hands, many wonderful sights, many different types of clothes, and many different weapons lifted. People are ready to kill each other, but there are not separate people here. One being, in his Supreme form -- I see all of that all at once.
Divya Mallya Ambaradharam -- he continues because he doesnt know where to start and where to end. He said, many mouths, all of this, and not only that, but Im seeing Divya Mallya Ambaradharam. Typically the things we notice: divine garlands, divine clothes. Divya Gandhanulaipanam -- with very divine fragrance. All the lepas, the pastes you apply. Obviously in our culture there is a lot of paste-applying, so very different types of paste.
Sarva Ascharimayam Devam Anantam Vishwato Mukham -- everything is so fascinating. Theres nothing normal about it. I cant say, Remember last time we went to such-and-such, and it was something similar. I cant do that. There is no experience I can relate to this vision of the Supreme. Thats why he is grabbing a word from here and a perception from there and just throwing it at Dhritarashtra, saying, Thats what Arjuna is experiencing right now.
I dont know whether you can comprehend or not. Divya Mallya Ambaradharam Sarva Aschariyamayam Devam Anantam -- this divine vision is Anantham, infinite. Its not something I can say starts here and ends here. Arjuna wanted to see the cosmic form in Krishna. He says, show me your cosmic form. Krishna obviously is finite.
He stands here and Arjuna stands here and the army is all around him. Its not that this vision is limited to the form of Krishna, however tall he was. This is infinite. What Arjuna is seeing is infinite. There is no end to it. There is no beginning he can see.
There is no end he can see. All he sees is hundreds and thousands of mouths, legs, clothes, malas, lamps, weapons, and wonderful sights. Everything is fascinating. I have nothing I can explain to you. Anandam Vishwa Tomukham -- facing all sides. Vishwa, the cosmos, is facing everywhere. In other words, this is something that cannot be limited to Krishnas being.
This vision is beyond any perception that we have ever had. As we have been discussing in Bhagavad Gita, the simple quest in life for any being is to exist. This is the basic instinct. What we want to preserve out of everything else is our existence. Therefore, this fear of death -- that my existence is temporary, that it began at my birth (time T1) and will end at my death (time T2).
And as I always say, those two events are hypothetical. Nobody has ever experienced their own birth and death. But I have come to this conclusion from inferences, Anumana. I have seen other people being born and I have seen other people dying. Therefore, I have come to the conclusion that my existence is temporary. Remember the very old song.
Maybe Anil will remember. Ae zindagi ki mele e zindagi ki melee Dunyame kam nahonge upsource. Hum nahonge upsource. I wish I will be there, but I will not be there. All this wonderful world will continue and I wish I would be there, but I will not be there. Thats my biggest fear.
Thats my essential quest in life to exist. And then we heard from Bhagavan in last few chapters.

These verses mark the pivotal moment when Krishna grants Arjuna the divine vision and Sanjaya begins narrating what unfolds. Krishna declares: Here in Me living as one, O Arjuna, behold the whole universe, movable and immovable. The key insight is that we normally see ourselves as observers separate from what we observe. The moment the ego was born in us - that first thought of this is me - we excluded ourselves from everything else. To see unity, this sense of separation must temporarily dissolve.
Think about how you constantly position yourself as an observer of life rather than a participant in its wholeness. When watching news of a disaster, do you feel that is happening to them, not me? When celebrating anothers success, is there a subtle sense of their gain, not mine? This observer-observed split is the fundamental illusion Krishna is removing from Arjunas perception. The divine vision combines all things into one - not by changing the world, but by changing the way of seeing.
For todays practice, experiment with dissolving the observer-observed boundary. When you look at a tree, instead of thinking I am seeing the tree, try experiencing seeing is happening. When in conversation, rather than I am listening to you, sense simply listening is occurring. This subtle shift - from I doing something to simply experiencing awareness itself - offers a glimpse of what it means to see the universe living as one within the divine. Notice what changes when you are no longer the separate observer but simply awareness witnessing itself.
